item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
What a twist!!

I'm not sure I agree that this doesn't match up brilliantly with the source article, tbh. Sure, the kid must have some anomalous properties about him/her in order to survive down there so long, and we already know there's enough spatial warping in that staircase to explain why the kid crawling up doesn't translate to them getting closer to the D-Bois.

I think my favorite thing is that this was able to offer more information while still raising new questions and leaving others unanswered.

+1 pho sho'

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This doesn't quite match with the article itself, but I still find it rather compelling. I always liked the ambiguous relation between the face and the voice (plus the face's lack of any clear harmful nature - sure, it's freaky and seems to chase you, but it doesn't actually do anything on camera beyond just keep trying to get closer). Plus it has that nice little question of what, exactly, this thing seeking help is - maybe it is a child of some sort, but no typical human child survives down there for so long.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
That guy never seemed particularly hostile to me either. It makes sense that he's trying to help the kid (or whatever the climber is) but can't communicate with (adult) humans.
Have my first ever +1!

I don't think that would happen if the source were moving towards the various explorations.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I like the re-imagining of 87, in theory. But this just doesn't work for me.
I can't jibe the observations of 87 from its article with what happens here. Particularly, the crier reaching the top of the stairs does not have the right feel.

The story is a square peg and my established impression of 87 is a round hole. For all that's a well-crafted peg.
